title: Radian Measure and Why Calculus Demands It
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Explain what radian measure means geometrically, convert 180 degrees to radians, and justify why calculus formulas for trigonometric functions assume radians.
finalAnswer: One radian is the angle whose intercepted arc equals the radius ($s = r\theta$); $180^\circ = \pi$ radians. Calculus uses radians because limits like $\lim_{\theta \to 0} \sin\theta/\theta = 1$, and hence $\tfrac{d}{dx}\sin x = \cos x$, hold only in radian measure.

steps.title: Define the Radian Geometrically
steps.explanation: The radian measure of a central angle is the ratio of the intercepted arc length to the radius, theta = s/r. A full circle of arc 2*pi*r corresponds to 2*pi radians, so 180 degrees, a half turn, equals pi radians.
steps.why: Defining angle as an arc-to-radius ratio is what makes theta a pure dimensionless number, ready for calculus.

steps.title: Examine the Fundamental Limit
steps.explanation: The squeeze-theorem proof compares the areas of triangles and sectors, which requires arc length to equal radius times angle. In degrees this limit becomes 180/pi, since one degree subtends pi/180 of the radian arc.
steps.why: Every derivative of every trig function is built from this single limit, so its radian-dependence propagates everywhere.

steps.title: See the Cost of Using Degrees
steps.explanation: If x were interpreted as degrees, each differentiation of sine or cosine would drag along a factor of pi/180. Series expansions, integrals, and the elegant solutions of differential equations like y'' = -y would all accumulate the same clutter.
steps.why: Radians are the unit that keeps the calculus of circular functions clean, which is why textbooks silently assume them.
